title: Telemetry playbook scrap notes — midday ops
content:
Context:
Short midday capture after the 11/03 ops sync. This is a loose, scratchpad-style record for the telemetry playbook iteration — not final. Built from voice notes and a whiteboard photo (see confluence link above).

Attendees (quick):
- Nina (note taker)
- Marco (telemetry lead)
- Priya (UX rollouts)
- Ethan (analytics infra)
- Tasha (SRE — joined briefly)

High-level aim:
- Make the canary telemetry playbook actionable for PMs and on-call: what to look at, quick triage steps, and safe rollback thresholds. Focus: panel UI rollouts + analytics pipeline changes scheduled next week.

Top threads and decisions:
1) Canary thresholds: set initial latency/err-rate guardrails for panel rollout.
   - Decision: start with 99th pct latency increase > 25% for 5m OR error rate > 1.5x baseline for 10m triggers an alert.
   - Rationale: conservative but avoids noisy blips; we can tighten later.
   - Owner: Marco to codify in alert policy (JIRA-OBS-2031).

2) Instrumentation gaps discovered during dry-run:
   - Missing route-level tokenization metrics for new panel preview flow. Hard to attribute cost/latency tradeoffs without it.
   - Action: Ethan to add a lightweight metric (panel.preview.tokens) that tags by model and route. Minimal cardinality (model, route, environment). Due: 2027-11-06.

3) Canary traffic split and fallback plan:
   - Split: 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 3 hours if stable.
   - Fallback: automatic rollback to previous variant on two consecutive critical alerts OR manual rollback if PM flags UX regression.
   - Note: Role of console feature flag needs clearer documentation. Priya to draft short “how to toggle and observe” section in console docs. Due: 2027-11-05.

4) Dashboard quick-views for on-call:
   - Build a single-row dashboard for each canary with: p99 latency (trend sparkline), request rate, error rate, top 3 error messages, and token spend delta.
   - Ethan proposes using the new summary-widget (low-cardinality). Prototype link: github PR (linked above).
   - Owner: Ethan + Marco to ship prototype by 2027-11-08.

5) Cost signal sanity check:
   - We saw a 12% token-cost bump in internal test load for panel preview due to tokenization differences. Need baseline comparison across models.
   - Quick task: Nina to run a 1k-scenario tokenization diff script and share results in the rollout channel. Due: EOD 2027-11-04.

Open questions / Known unknowns:
- How aggressive should automatic rollback be for subtle UX regressions (e.g., hallucination rates)? We lack a robust automatic hallucination detector.
- Can we reuse existing KV cache hit metrics as a proxy for prompt prefix reuse across routes? (Marco to validate with infra ops.)
- Is the summary-widget going to be supported in the on-call mobile view? If not, we need a fallback single-metric alert route.

Quick snippets from the whiteboard (notes to self):
- "If p99 spikes but p50 stable -> likely one-off large prompt (check tokens)"
- "Tag canary requests with x-rollout-id and x-rollout-step -> helps causal tracing"
- "Add a small synthetic ping every 15s from canary group to measure cold-start variance"

Action items (concrete):
- Marco: write and attach alert thresholds to JIRA-OBS-2031; include rollback wiring notes. (Due 2027-11-05)
- Ethan: add panel.preview.tokens metric (low cardinality), prototype summary dashboard (PR linked). (Add tests, due 2027-11-08)
- Priya: document how to toggle flags and where to look for UX regressions — include screenshots. (Due 2027-11-05)
- Nina: run token-diff script and post results to #console-rollouts (EOD 2027-11-04).
- Tasha (SRE): validate rollback automation in staging (rehearse on 2027-11-06).

Quick checklist for canary day (short):
- [ ] Confirm instrumentation deployed to staging
- [ ] Confirm dashboard template populated for on-call
- [ ] Run synthetic load + token-diff baseline
- [ ] Rehearse rollback once with SRE
- [ ] Send PM and CS short note with expectations

Meeting adjourn notes / tone:
- Felt like we have a practical set of steps and conservative thresholds; the key risk is visibility holes. Keep telemetry changes tiny and add more metrics only where they give clear signal.
- This doc remains a scratchpad — will convert to a short playbook summary after action items close.

Relevant links / artifacts (repeat for visibility):
- Jira: JIRA-ENG-1427 (panel rollout epic)
- Alerts ticket: JIRA-OBS-2031
- Confluence whiteboard: https://confluence.redwood/company/console-rollouts
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/987

Unresolved / parking lot:
- Ownership for hallucination experiments (who can run evals quickly on canary traffic?) -> park with research for now.
- Need a short FAQ for PMs: "When do we roll back vs iterate?" Priya to draft.

If anything missing or if you want a different format (timeline, checklist-first), say so — will reformat before turning into the playbook.
